usedBy.name: React Native
usedBy.note: Uses the C++ Yoga engine, not the Rust bindings.

features.name: Horizontal and vertical stacks
features.note: Row and column flows. This does not imply CSS flexbox conformance.

features.name: CSS flexbox
features.note: Morphorm uses stretch units. Torin uses its own flex content and sizing model. Yoga has some defaults that differ from browsers. ui_layout implements an experimental flexbox-inspired model, not full CSS compatibility. Clay uses its own fit/grow sizing model, without CSS flexbox conformance or weighted grow factors. Ply implements a Clay-inspired model with weighted grow sizing and wrapping, not full CSS flexbox conformance. Keru Layout uses dependency-graph solving with weighted Fill sizes, not CSS flexbox. hooke implements CSS Flexbox Level 1, but not vertical writing modes, last-baseline alignment, visibility: collapse, or calc(). Backer distributes space using its own constraints and equal expansion model, without CSS flexbox or unequal grow weights.

features.name: CSS grid
features.note: Morphorm exposes grid tracks and spans, not the complete CSS grid model. Keru Layout has uniform grid cells and spans, not CSS grid tracks. Torin, Yoga, Clay, Ply, Backer, and hooke do not support CSS grid. The pinned ui_layout Git revision implements an experimental grid subset.

features.name: Wrapping flow
features.note: Native flow wrapping, with different sizing semantics between libraries. ui_layout wrapping is available in the pinned Git revision. Clay supports text wrapping, but not automatic wrapping of child elements. Backer and Keru Layout have stacks, but no automatic child-flow wrapping. Keru Layout's uniform grid is not a wrapping stack.

features.name: Fixed and percentage sizes
features.note: Explicit sizes and sizes relative to the containing area. Backer supports fixed sizes but has no native parent-percentage dimension. Its dynamic sizing callbacks receive the opposite-axis size, not the parent size on the same axis.

features.name: Content-based sizing
features.note: Size a container from its contents.

features.name: Padding and gaps
features.note: Inner spacing and spacing between children.

features.name: In-flow margins
features.note: Morphorm's edge spacing applies to absolute nodes, not in-flow margins. Clay, Ply, Backer, and Keru Layout have padding and gaps, but no in-flow margin property. These adapters skip margin templates.

features.name: Aspect ratio property
features.note: Torin and ui_layout adapters skip ratio templates because the benchmarked versions have no aspect-ratio style property. ui_layout can apply ratios through custom-object sizing, which is not the same as a general node style property. Backer provides aspect_width and aspect_height, but the shared ratio workload is skipped because it also requires percentages.

features.name: Custom content measurement
features.note: Taffy has a measurement callback, Morphorm has Node::content_size, Torin has LayoutMeasurer, Yoga has a measure function, and ui_layout has CustomLayouter. Cephal has compute_layout_with_measure, and hooke has the Measure trait for measured leaves. Backer offers dynamic_width and dynamic_height measurement callbacks. These hooks are not built-in text shaping or text measurement engines. Clay, Ply, and Keru Layout expose text measurement callbacks, not general arbitrary-content measurement hooks.

features.name: CSS block layout
features.note: Taffy, Cephal, and ui_layout implement CSS-style block formatting. Morphorm, Torin, Clay, Ply, Backer, and Keru Layout stacks are not CSS block layout. Yoga and hooke are flexbox engines without CSS block layout.

features.name: Pixel-grid rounding
features.note: Taffy, Cephal, and Yoga round layout output to a pixel grid. Morphorm rounds some percentage sizes and stretch allocations, but does not guarantee pixel-aligned output for all coordinates. Torin has scaling helpers but no built-in output-snapping pass. ui_layout's round() length expression does not round all layout output. Clay, Ply, Backer, and Keru Layout compute floating-point dimensions and positions without a pixel-grid rounding pass. hooke leaves layout output unrounded and provides a snap function that the host applies to each frame at mount time.

features.name: Incremental measuring
features.note: Reuse unchanged measurements across layout passes and remeasure affected nodes. Taffy, Cephal, and Yoga cache layout results with dirty-node invalidation. hooke caches results in each node and invalidates them through style keys, measured-leaf content ids, and mutable access to children. Torin tracks dirty nodes and their layout dependencies. Morphorm recomputes the tree on each layout pass. ui_layout caches intrinsic layout results but has no public invalidation API. Clay and Ply cache text measurements, but rebuild element layout each frame rather than incrementally measuring a retained tree. Backer runs full resolve and allocation passes, without dirty-node invalidation. Keru Layout incrementally solves non-structural changes in cycle-free layouts, falling back to a full solve for structural changes.
